sentences.text: Eggerthella lenta is a gut Actinobacterium that inactivates the cardiac drug digoxin.
A cytochrome-encoding operon up-regulated by digoxin is absent from non-metabolising strains and was predictive of digoxin inactivation by the human gut microbiome.
In gnotobiotic mice, dietary protein was reported to reduce microbial metabolism of digoxin, with changes in drug concentration in serum and urine.
Strains oxidise and epimerise bile acid hydroxyl groups; a human fecal isolate carried 3-alpha, 3-beta, 7-alpha and 12-alpha hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity.
A study reporting a cohort of patients with E. lenta bacteremia described it as an emerging pathogen, and most of those patients had serious intra-abdominal pathology.
